Gold Purity Testing in Noida & Greater Noida West — Free XRF Test

Before you sell gold — or even before you buy it — know exactly what you have. Our German XRF Karatmeter tests your gold's purity in seconds, in front of you, with zero damage. Why Purity Testing Decides What You're Paid

Every rupee of a gold valuation flows from one number: purity. Payout = weight × purity × live rate — so a buyer who reads your 22K chain as 'about 18K' has cut roughly a fifth of your money with a single assumption. That is why the testing method matters more than the shop's promises. A proper XRF (X-ray fluorescence) Karatmeter analyses the metal's composition directly and displays the percentages — gold, silver, copper and other alloys — on a screen you read yourself.

Testing is equally useful when you are not selling: verifying an inherited piece, checking a gift, confirming a hallmark before a wedding purchase, or settling a family division fairly. Bring the piece in — the test is free in all these cases.

Karat and Purity — Quick Reference

BIS hallmark numbers state purity in parts per thousand. Here is what the common karats actually mean:

KaratPurityHallmarkTypically
24K99.9%999Coins & bars
22K91.6%916Most Indian jewellery
18K75.0%750Diamond jewellery
14K58.5%585Lightweight / imported pieces

XRF vs Acid vs Touchstone

The older methods survive because they are cheap and because their vagueness benefits the tester. Acid and touchstone tests damage the surface and produce a range, not a reading — and that range is always interpreted by the person paying you. Melting gives a true answer but destroys the piece, so it can only happen after you've committed. XRF is the only method that is simultaneously exact, instant and reversible: if you don't like the valuation, your jewellery is untouched and leaves with you.

MethodDamages Jewellery?AccuracyResult Shown to You?
XRF Karatmeter (ours)No — non-destructiveExact composition readingYes — live on screen
Acid testYes — surface reactionEstimate onlyRarely verifiable
TouchstoneYes — scratches the pieceEstimate onlyNo
Melting & assayDestroys the pieceAccurate but irreversibleAfter the fact
